Sofia / Marcus — please see legal take below. I also attached a redline with two alternative compromise positions (redline_msa_priyom_v2.docx).

Summary / recommended approach (short):
1) Do not accept an unlimited carve-out as drafted. That exposes Redwood to infinite liability for routine/accidental incidents.
2) Offer a targeted carve-out that: (a) excludes from the cap only proven, willful misappropriation of trade secrets and (b) limits other confidentiality breaches to direct damages capped at a multiple of fees or a fixed floor.
3) Require objective proof, and if injunctive relief is sought, tie it to a judicial determination or binding arbitration finding that trade-secret misappropriation occurred.

Suggested draft language (for negotiation):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitation of liability set forth in Section X shall not apply to liabilities arising from (i) willful and proven misappropriation of trade secrets by Supplier, or (ii) Customer's confidential data disclosure resulting from Supplier's gross negligence or willful misconduct; provided that such liabilities shall be limited to direct monetary damages up to the greater of (A) three (3) times the aggregate Fees paid by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the event, or (B) One Million United States Dollars (USD 1,000,000), unless a final court or arbitral award determines that higher damages are appropriate for willful trade-secret misappropriation."
Rationale: this preserves our policy of predictable liability while giving customers comfort for truly egregious conduct. It also creates an objective proof standard (willful + proven) and a reasonable upper bound so we don't lose insurability.

Commercial fallback: if LedgerBank insists on unlimited exclusion, escalate to execs for approval and a pricing concession (we would require a 20% increase to list for that change). As a negotiation concession, we can offer the above language plus a 10% one-time implementation credit.

Operational asks: confirm whether LedgerBank requires real-time breach notification SLA, plus details on the categories of data they consider "trade secrets" (we should avoid an overly broad definition).

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful — I can join with our security lead.

Amelia / John —

Thanks for the note and for sharing the redline. We value LedgerBank's security requirements and want to find a pragmatic path forward. After internal review, Redwood can make the following counterproposal:

1) We will accept a limited carve-out for confidentiality breaches that meet a high standard (willful misappropriation of trade secrets or disclosure resulting from gross negligence).

2) To balance predictability and customer protection, liabilities that fall within this narrow carve-out will be capped at the greater of (a) three (3) times the aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months or (b) USD 1,000,000, except where a final court or arbitral award determines higher damages for willful trade-secret theft.

3) We will agree to expedited notification (24 hours) and to cooperate with LedgerBank's forensic process, subject to our security and privacy policies.

As a commercial concession, Redwood is willing to provide a one-time implementation credit equal to 10% of year-one fees if LedgerBank will accept the limited carve-out above and the accompanying standard of proof.

I have attached a redlined MSA with the proposed language highlighted (MSA_BigBank_Redline_v3.docx). Please let us know whether this is acceptable or if you need changes to the proof/forensic language. If LedgerBank insists on an unlimited exclusion, we will need executive approval and a revised pricing proposal.

Could you confirm by COB Friday whether you can accept this compromise? If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call with Priyom and our security lead to walk through the wording.

Thanks —
